title.value: Wake Up Digital Forensics' Community and Help Combat Ransomware

authors.value: Shaked, A.; Cherdantseva, Y.; Burnap, P.; Maynard, P.

journal.value: IEEE Security & Privacy, vol. 20, issue 4, pp. 61-70 (Jul.-Aug. 2022)

quartile_sjr.value: Q1 (best quartile in Law per SCImago 2022, SJR 2022 = 0.684) - venue met the Q1/Q2 eligibility threshold at publication year
Q1 (SCImago 2023: Q1 in Computer Science (miscellaneous) and Law)

source_database.value: IEEE Xplore; verified via IEEE Computer Society Digital Library metadata

study_type.value: Position/best-practice article on procedural countermeasures and digital forensics for ransomware (grounded in comparative case analysis of companies' ransomware strategies)
Conceptual contribution / system design with case-study evaluation (novel playbook mechanism plus open-source tool demonstration)

methodology.value: Argumentative best-practice synthesis supported by a comparative analysis of implemented ransomware strategies of companies (extended Rhine valley region, first author's related thesis work); examines technical vs procedural countermeasures and the role of digital forensics in ransomware investigation and preparation; makes recommendations for sharing detailed incident case studies

Identifies the conceptual gap that current playbook research/practice represent playbooks as process models that cannot communicate operational impact of an incident or of the response; proposes operations-informed playbooks by embedding a model of operations (dependency map) into the playbook's process model and linking IR activities with operational context; introduces a new metric for evaluating change in operations in coordination with critical thresholds for IR decision-making; demonstrates the approach via a ransomware attack IR playbook case study using a newly developed open-source tool

key_findings.value: Organizations, literature, and research efforts focus on technical measures and neglect procedural countermeasures against ransomware; detailed case studies and shared best practices are needed so companies can adapt strategies and be better prepared; the digital forensics community has an underused role in combating ransomware

Playbook design currently lacks the ability to communicate operational impact of an incident and of incident response on the organization; embedding an operations model into playbooks reflects interdependencies and mutual influences of IR activities and operations in an accurate, systematic way; a new operations-change metric with critical thresholds supports decision-making during ransomware response; demonstrated in a ransomware IR case study using an open-source tool

limitations.value: Position-style article with claims grounded in a regional (extended Rhine valley) comparative analysis of limited scope; no systematic evaluation of countermeasure effectiveness; recommendations are qualitative and practitioner-oriented

Conceptual approach demonstrated in a single ransomware case study; no enterprise field deployment or multi-organization evaluation; adoption effort/costs of modeling operations itself are acknowledged as a practical consideration

research_gaps.value: Identifies the neglect of procedural countermeasures and of digital-forensic readiness in the ransomware defense literature; highlights the absence of shared, detailed incident case studies and best practices that organizations can adopt

Identifies a significant conceptual gap in cybersecurity playbook design research and practice: inability to communicate operational impact of incidents and of incident response; proposes closing it via operations-informed playbooks that link process models to models of operations

inclusion_rationale.value: Passes eligibility: published July-August 2022 (2022-2026 window); IEEE Security & Privacy held SCImago Q1 (best quartile, Law) with SJR 0.684 in 2022; indexed on IEEE Xplore (allowed source); retained as the designated forensic-readiness candidate paper

Passes eligibility: published November 2023 (2022-2026 window); Computers & Security at SCImago Q1 in 2023; hosted on ScienceDirect (allowed source); retained as the designated operations-informed playbook candidate paper

platform_environment.value: Windows/enterprise IT (organizational forensic readiness across company environments)
Windows/enterprise IT with critical national infrastructure framing (operations dependency context; Colonial Pipeline-style fuel-supply impact scenario discussed)

kill_chain_stage.value: Pre-encryption (forensic readiness and procedural preparation) and post-encryption (forensic investigation after impact)
Pre-encryption (playbook preparation stage) and post-encryption (response decision-making amid operational degradation)

dataset_benchmark.value: No dataset; draws on comparative analysis of companies' implemented countermeasures and public case sources; no open dataset
No empirical dataset; artifact is a newly developed open-source tool implementing the operations-informed playbook approach, demonstrated on a ransomware IR playbook case study

evaluation_metrics.value: Qualitative case-study evaluation; proposes a novel metric for evaluating change in operations in coordination with critical thresholds during response - an operational impact measure rather than detection-style F1/latency metrics; no quantitative external validation

reproducibility.value: Low: argumentative synthesis without controlled experiments or benchmark environments
Moderate-to-good conceptually: open-source tool supports replication of the case-study demonstration, but metric validation is qualitative and there is no external sandbox/production comparison
